item.title: Research (Trial): Can a test catch the fixed tab bar covering page content, without a real phone?
item.description: Partly. Safe-area insets are 0 on rectangular screens, so desktop and CI browsers never see the notch case; only a device or simulator does. What a static test can guard is our own math: body padding-bottom is 4.5rem and the bar is about 3.5rem (52px links plus padding and border). No test checks that the gap holds today. Pitch: a small test that fails if the bar outgrows the body padding.

item.title: Research (Shield): Can a script-free GitHub Pages site set a useful Content-Security-Policy, and is it worth it?
item.description: Yes, partly. Pages sends no CSP header, but a meta CSP works for script controls. Our built pages have no script tags, inline handlers or javascript: links, so script-src 'none' with object-src and base-uri 'none' would block injected script at no cost. frame-ancestors can't be set by meta, and 51 pages use style attributes, so leave style-src alone. Pitch for standup.

item.title: Research (Critic): Challenge: does the Polish tab-bar pitch (viewport-fit=cover) fix a real problem?
item.description: Probably not as written. Without viewport-fit=cover, Safari already insets the page inside the safe area, so env() being 0 is expected, not a bug. Turning cover on is what lets content run under the corners and sensor, and then every edge needs inset padding, including landscape sides. Hold the cover change until a phone screenshot shows overlap; scroll-padding-bottom can be judged on its own.

item.title: Research (Polish): Does our new five-tab bottom bar follow current guidance for web tab bars on phones?
item.description: Mostly yes: named nav of links, aria-current, visible labels, 52px targets, body padding. Two gaps: no viewport-fit=cover, so env(safe-area-inset-bottom) is 0 on notched iPhones and the bar can sit on the home indicator; no scroll-padding-bottom, so jump links or focus can land under the bar. Pitch: add both on phones; check landscape side insets first.

item.title: Research (Pixel): Should our long pages use content-visibility: auto now that it is Baseline?
item.description: Not yet. content-visibility is Baseline newly available since Sept 15, 2025, but one measured test found the one-line snippet made a 200-item page slower; it only paid off on long lists with a measured contain-intrinsic-size. Our longest page today is Receipts at about 64 KB, so the win is unproven. No pitch; revisit only if a page grows long enough to measure a gain.

item.title: Research (Advocate): What are readers publicly struggling with about Grok Bot this month?
item.description: Loudest November problem is usage: meters jumping to 100% around Nov 1, a weekly-limit reset for all users on Nov 9, and an efficiency update (about 7% more usage, up to 15% on routines). A forum thread reports bots not replying on Nov 13, stopped Nov 14. None is in our known issues. Pitch: Scout and Verify trace these to official sources first.
